note.question: How should fewer suppliers be assigned as ad hoc as the pool size increases?
note.overview: Inspired by India’s challenges in importing pulses, we study the negotiation of government-to-government food importing contracts, with a focus on ad hoc and forward negotiations with multiple suppliers (henceforth referred to as multiple-sourcing negotiations). We are the first to comprehensively study ad hoc and forward multiple-sourcing negotiations for food importing. Such problems are widespread, especially in developing nations, and thus the research can be relevant to the wellbeing of large underprivileged populations.

Such problems are widespread, especially in developing nations, and thus the research can be relevant to the wellbeing of large underprivileged populations.

Such leverage would not impact the negotiation outcomes if there are many forward suppliers who already serve as leverage against one another, but when there are relatively few forward suppliers, the existence of the ad hoc suppliers will in- ﬂuence the negotiation outcomes.

We assume the buyer’s internal production cost is lower than that of all suppliers and normalize it to zero to ensure that the buyer ﬁrst attempts to meet the demand with its entire internal capacity.
